units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Practical stuff. What's the vibe?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A city of cafés and small museums, and the weather is changeable.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Carry a light jacket. The center is quite walkable, with cobbled streets and hills, so wear good shoes.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the food everybody talks about?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Belgian beer culture was recognized by UNESCO in 2016.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Chocolate, waffles, and fries are everywhere.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the praline is traditionally credited to a Brussels chocolatier named Neuhaus, who has a shop in the Galeries.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Tourist traps?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The streets right around the Grand Place can be crowded and pricey.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Walk two or three streets away and you'll usually find something better.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And if it rains?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then go indoors, and Brussels is good at that.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Galeries are covered. There are museums.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And a lot of cafés that exist just to give you somewhere to wait the weather out.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So what's the one thing to take away from all this?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That Brussels gets knocked down and rebuilt, and keeps its sense of humor.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A small boy on a fountain, in a different costume every week, tells you most of it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Right. Go have a good day.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And if you want the whole story, the long episode will be waiting for you tonight.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And if it rains?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then you've got the Galeries, and a very good waffle.
